recipes.title: Polish pork cutlets with cabbage, light
recipes.summary: Crisp Polish-style pork cutlets with boiled potatoes and tender cabbage. Extra cabbage and lighter breading keep the lunch lean while the pork remains generous.

steps.instruction: Prepare the pork loin, potato, green cabbage and onion in their listed forms.
Pulse the bread in a food processor until coarse crumbs form.
Pound each loin cutlet to an even thickness.
Season the loin with the paprika and half the salt.
Simmer the potato until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Cook the onion in the butter until soft and lightly golden.
Cook the green cabbage with the onion until tender and lightly browned.
Mash the potato with the whole milk until smooth.
Arrange the wheat flour, eggs and bread crumbs in separate shallow dishes.
Coat each loin cutlet evenly in the wheat flour.
Dip each floured loin cutlet into the eggs.
Press each loin cutlet firmly into the bread crumbs.
Heat the olive oil in a wide frying pan.
Fry the pork cutlets until the first side is deeply golden.
Turn the pork cutlets and cook until the second side is golden and the centre is cooked through.
Rest the pork cutlets so the juices settle.
Serve the pork cutlets with the potato and green cabbage.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the pork cutlets, potatoes and cabbage separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the cutlets in a hot oven or dry pan. Freeze the cooked cutlets for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Vegan lentil sloppy joes, light
recipes.summary: Saucy red lentils, peppers and carrots piled onto toasted bread in a tangy American tomato sauce. Extra vegetables and less bread keep this vegan dinner lighter.

steps.instruction: Prepare the onion, bell pepper, carrot, garlic and bread in their listed forms.
Rinse the red lentils under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and carrot until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and tomato paste until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, vegetable broth, red lentils, brown sugar and salt.
Simmer the filling until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick enough to mound on bread.
Toast the bread until crisp around the edges.
Rest the sloppy joe filling so it thickens slightly.
Spoon the lentil filling generously over the toasted bread.
Serve the vegan lentil sloppy joes while hot.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the lentil filling for up to 4 days and the bread separately. Reheat the filling with a splash of vegetable broth and toast fresh bread. Freeze the filling for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Vegetarian full English traybake, light
recipes.summary: A lighter vegetarian full English with baked eggs, mushrooms, beans, spinach, tomatoes and crisp potatoes. Extra vegetables and less bread keep the breakfast generous.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Prepare the potato, mushrooms, onion and bread in their listed forms.
Coat the potato and onion with the olive oil, paprika and salt.
Roast the potato and onion until they begin to turn golden.
Add the mushrooms and butter to the tray.
Roast until the mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir the white beans into the tomatoes in a small ovenproof dish.
Place the bean dish on the roasting tray.
Bake until the white beans and tomatoes are bubbling.
Scatter the spinach across the hot vegetables.
Make shallow wells between the vegetables.
Crack the eggs into the wells.
Bake until the egg whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.
Toast the bread until crisp and golden.
Serve the vegetarian full English traybake with the toast.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served immediately while the eggs are tender. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat gently. Store the toast separately. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: German cabbage soup with cured pork, light
recipes.summary: A lighter German cabbage soup with cured pork, potatoes, leeks and root vegetables in a thyme-scented broth. Extra cabbage keeps the lunch generous.

steps.instruction: Prepare the cured pork, potato, green cabbage, leek, carrot, celery, onion and garlic in their listed forms.
Melt the butter in a large soup pot over medium heat.
Cook the cured pork until browned around the edges.
Cook the onion, leek, carrot and celery until softened.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir until fragrant.
Add the green cabbage, potato, beef stock and salt.
Simmer the soup until the potato and cabbage are tender.
Stir the sour cream into a ladle of hot broth until smooth.
Return the cream mixture to the soup.
Simmer the soup gently until creamy and evenly hot.
Rest the German cabbage soup off the heat.
Serve the soup with the cured pork distributed evenly between bowls.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and reheat gently without boiling hard so the sour cream stays smooth. Freeze before adding the cream for up to 3 months.

recipes.title: Chicken saag, light
recipes.summary: Tender chicken breast in a smooth spinach, tomato, ginger and cumin sauce with a modest serving of rice. Extra spinach keeps this high-protein Indian dinner light.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Cook the white rice until tender, then keep it covered so the grains finish steaming.
Prepare the chicken breast, spinach, onion, garlic and ginger in their listed forms.
Heat the olive oil in a wide saucepan over medium-high heat.
Brown the chicken breast until lightly coloured on several sides.
Transfer the breast pieces to a plate.
Cook the onion until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, paprika and salt and stir until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and chicken stock to the onion mixture.
Simmer the sauce until the tomatoes soften and the liquid reduces slightly.
Fold the spinach into the sauce until fully wilted.
Blend the spinach sauce until smooth.
Return the spinach sauce to the saucepan.
Stir the greek yogurt into the sauce until creamy.
Return the chicken breast to the sauce.
Simmer until the breast is cooked through and the saag is thick and glossy.
Rest the chicken saag off the heat so the flavours settle.
Serve the chicken saag with the white rice.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate the chicken saag and rice separately for up to 3 days. Reheat gently until steaming. Freeze for up to 1 month, accepting that the yogurt sauce may need stirring after thawing.
